claims.text: The feedstock is pre-alloyed AlCrFeNiSi powder optimized for additive manufacturing.
Ultrashort pulsed laser melting can replace continuous-wave or long-pulse laser melting in powder bed fusion of AlCrFeNiSi.
The proposed laser operates in the femtosecond-to-picosecond pulse-duration regime.
Ultrashort pulses provide localized, rapid energy deposition during melting.
The proposed process is applicable to miniature components with dimensions below 10 mm.
The process can be tuned to achieve cooling rates on the order of 10^6 K/s while ensuring full consolidation.
The proposed process produces an ultra-refined microstructure with reduced grain size.
The proposed process produces lower dislocation densities.
Reduced grain sizes and lower dislocation densities mediate a reduction in residual stress.
Ultrashort pulses melt only the localized volumes necessary for consolidation.
Localized ultrashort-pulse melting limits heat diffusion into surrounding material.
Limited heat diffusion sharply reduces thermal gradients.
Rapid solidification minimizes residual stress and produces a more homogeneous microstructure.
Compared with conventional high-thermal-load processing, ultrashort-pulse processing will lower residual thermal stresses in AlCrFeNiSi components.
Compared with conventional high-thermal-load processing, ultrashort-pulse processing will increase microhardness and improve tensile characteristics.
Ultrashort-pulse processing will reduce the need for extensive post-build stress relief.
Conventional continuous-wave or long-pulse laser powder bed fusion typically produces high residual stresses in these components.
Prolonged heat exposure in conventional processing degrades microstructural uniformity and mechanical properties.
